title: Informal Conjecture (Section 1.2): dropping bounded-degree assumption
statement_text: The authors prove that subgraph-closed graph classes with strongly sublinear separators and bounded maximum degree admit thin systems of overlays. It seems plausible that the additional assumption of bounded maximum degree could be dropped, i.e. that every subgraph-closed class with strongly sublinear separators admits thin systems of overlays, leading to a much more general result strengthening the majority of the known approximation algorithms (Baker-type, bidimensionality-based, local search) that the authors survey.
context_text: An overlay of a graph $G$ is a triple $(H,f,\ell)$ where $H$ is a graph, $f:V(H)\to V(G)$ is a homomorphism and $\ell:V(H)\to\{0,1,2,\dots\}$; it is an $r$-neighborhood overlay if $\ell\le r$, every $v\in V(G)$ has a preimage $x$ with $\ell(x)=r$, and it is walk-preserving: for every $x$ with $\ell(x)\ge1$ and every neighbour $w$ of $f(x)$ in $G$, $x$ has a neighbour $y$ with $f(y)=w$ and $\ell(y)\ge\ell(x)-1$ (so the radius-$r$ neighbourhood of each vertex is faithfully represented). A system of overlays is a multiset $\mathcal{L}$ of them; its thickness is $\max_v\frac{1}{|\mathcal{L}|}\sum_{(H,f,\ell)\in\mathcal{L}}|f^{-1}(v)|$ and its treewidth the maximum treewidth of the graphs $H$. Roughly, a class admits thin systems of overlays if for all positive integers $r,k$ every $n$-vertex member has a system of $r$-neighborhood overlays of thickness at most $1+1/k$, treewidth bounded by a function $t(r,k)$, and size polynomial in some function $q(n)$ (for the classes considered $q(n)$ is constant or $e^{(\log\log n)^2}$), computable efficiently. Such systems generalize Baker's bounded-treewidth layerings and yield simple polynomial-time approximation schemes for maximum independent set, minimum dominating set and their distance-$r$ versions, $H$-matching, vertex cover, and some monotone MSO-expressible problems. A balanced separation of $G$ is a pair $(A,B)$ of edge-disjoint subgraphs with $A\cup B=G$ and $|V(A)\setminus V(B)|,|V(B)\setminus V(A)|\le 2|V(G)|/3$, of size $|V(A)\cap V(B)|$; a class has sublinear separators if every $n$-vertex member has one of size $o(n)$, and strongly sublinear separators if of size at most $cn^{\delta}$ for constants $c\ge1$, $\delta<1$ (for subgraph-closed classes this is equivalent to polynomial expansion, by Dvořák and Norin). The authors prove that all proper minor-closed classes, and all subgraph-closed classes with bounded maximum degree and strongly sublinear separators, admit thin systems of overlays (in the latter case with $q(n)=e^{(\log\log n)^2}$). Every class admitting thin systems of overlays is fractionally treewidth-fragile, and the authors note that even the simpler question (raised earlier by Dvořák) whether subgraph-closed classes with strongly sublinear separators are fractionally treewidth-fragile is open.

title: Open Problem (Section 1.2): APX-hardness on classes without sublinear separators
statement_text: It would be interesting to see whether this intuition can be made precise and for example show that the maximum independent set problem is APX-hard on any subgraph-closed class of graphs that does not have sublinear separators (or at least has exponential expansion).
context_text: A balanced separation of $G$ is a pair $(A,B)$ of edge-disjoint subgraphs with $A\cup B=G$ and $|V(A)\setminus V(B)|,|V(B)\setminus V(A)|\le 2|V(G)|/3$, of size $|V(A)\cap V(B)|$; a class has sublinear separators if every $n$-vertex member has one of size $o(n)$, and strongly sublinear separators if of size at most $cn^{\delta}$ for constants $c\ge1$, $\delta<1$ (for subgraph-closed classes this is equivalent to polynomial expansion, by Dvořák and Norin). The expansion of a class measures the maximum average degree of its bounded-depth minors as a function of the depth (polynomial, subexponential or exponential expansion); the class of 3-regular graphs has exponential expansion, and subexponential expansion implies sublinear separators. Maximum independent set (and minimum dominating set) is APX-hard already on graphs of bounded maximum degree, in particular on 3-regular graphs, so approximation schemes cannot extend to classes containing all 3-regular graphs. The authors give approximation schemes (via so-called thin systems of overlays, a generalization of Baker's bounded-treewidth layerings) for proper minor-closed classes and for bounded-degree subgraph-closed classes with strongly sublinear separators, and observe that every class admitting their decompositions has sublinear separators. They suggest that this intuition might be made precise, e.g. by showing APX-hardness of maximum independent set on every subgraph-closed class without sublinear separators, or at least on every such class with exponential expansion.
notes: Stated as an open research question in prose; no labelled theorem environment.
